name: Ransomware Closes Schools
description: Ransomware takes down the student information system, transportation routing, and food service; campuses close or run manual days during recovery.
asset: Student information, transportation, and food service systems
assumptions: Recovery takes 1–4 weeks with staggered campus restoration.
State attendance funding is unaffected by short closures.
Secondary loss covers notification and community-trust measures.

name: Student Data Breach
description: A phished staff account or a compromised SIS vendor exposes student records, including special-education and disciplinary data.
threat: Credential phishing crews or vendor compromise
assumptions: Minors' data raises notification and monitoring costs per record.
Vendor-held data is in scope; contract recovery is uncertain.
Secondary loss includes claims from affected families.

name: Payroll and Vendor Redirect Fraud
description: Fraudsters phish HR or impersonate vendors to redirect payroll deposits or construction-fund payments.
assumptions: Bond-program payments are the highest-value targets.
Bank recovery is reflected in the primary-loss estimates.
Secondary loss covers audit findings and board-mandated controls.

name: DDoS During State Testing Window
description: A denial-of-service attack (often student-initiated) disrupts online state assessments, forcing rescheduled testing sessions across campuses.
assumptions: Only attacks inside testing windows are loss events.
Primary loss covers makeup sessions, staffing, and mitigation services.

name: Staff W-2 Phishing Disclosure
description: A payroll-season phishing email tricks staff into disclosing W-2 or direct-deposit data, exposing employees to tax fraud.
assumptions: A loss event is disclosure of records for multiple employees.
Primary loss covers monitoring, notification, and HR time.
Secondary loss includes employee claims and union grievances.
